clips.start_words: Write down the six most important
clips.caption:
A consultant sat in a CEO's office for a month and didn't say a word.

Charles Schwab ran U.S. Steel, the largest company in the world, and he was overwhelmed. After watching him, Ivy Lee gave him one instruction: every night, write the six most important things you have to do tomorrow, in order. Work only on the first one until it's done. Then move to the second.

Schwab was skeptical, so Ivy Lee said to try it 60 days, then pay whatever he thought it was worth.

Thirty days later, Ivy Lee opened a check for $250,000 - over $5 million in today's money.

What would one focused list be worth to your business?

clips.end_words: into a phone or a computer
clips.caption:
Research Kevin Trudeau cites says typing on a keyboard activates around 9 neural pathways in your brain. Printing activates about 37.

Writing in cursive activates hundreds.

That's why he still writes his to-do list by hand, in cursive, after 40 years of running businesses. The more of your brain a task engages, the harder it is to forget - and the more your subconscious keeps working on it while you sleep.

Your phone is convenient. It just isn't doing what a pen does.

Have you tried writing your to-do list by hand this week?

#kevintrudeau #productivity #successhabits #mindset #businesstips #focus

Kevin Trudeau doesn't rank his to-do list by importance. He asks one question about every item.

Does this absolutely, positively have to happen today? If the answer is no, it's a B. If the answer is yes - which is rare - it's an A. Most days he ends up with only one or two A's, and everything else can wait.

Finish your A's by mid-morning and something happens psychologically: you feel like you're on top of the world, powerful, efficient. That win carries you into the B's with momentum instead of dread.

The list stops being a mountain and starts being a filter.

What's actually an A on your list today?

#kevintrudeau #productivity #successhabits #businesstips #mindset #timemanagement

Here's a common error Kevin Trudeau sees people make: writing everything they have to do onto one single to-do list for tomorrow.

You can't get it all done, so most of it just sits there making you feel like you failed.

His fix: before you write anything down, ask if it actually has to happen today. If it doesn't, flip ahead in your calendar to a day when it can, and write it there instead. Nothing goes on tomorrow's list unless tomorrow is genuinely when it belongs.

A daily list only works if it's actually daily - a handful of things, not everything.

How many things on your list today don't actually belong there?

#kevintrudeau #productivity #successhabits #businesstips #timemanagement #mindset

Kevin Trudeau keeps a tab for every important person in his life - alphabetized, A through Z, in the back of his planner.

The moment he thinks of something to tell one of them, he doesn't rely on memory. He flips to their tab and writes it down: discuss the price on this program, follow up on that deal. Then he closes it and moves on.

By the time they actually meet, nothing gets forgotten and nothing gets repeated. Every conversation just picks up exactly where the last one left off.

Who do you keep meaning to bring something up with?

#kevintrudeau #productivity #businesstips #successhabits #relationships #entrepreneur

We all have the exact same 24 hours. Kevin Trudeau says that's exactly why time management doesn't exist.

You can't manage time - it moves at the same speed for everyone, rich or broke. What you can manage is your activities, and which ones you actually make a priority.

He's used the same priority system for 40 years: no missed appointments, no forgotten tasks, no anxiety staring at a list. Not because he found more hours in the day. Because he stopped trying to.

When people say they're doing time management, Kevin Trudeau says it's a lie. You're managing your priorities, or you're managing nothing at all.
